newsitem.title: USA: U.S. will take part in Zaire rescue force - Perry.
newsitem.headline: U.S. will take part in Zaire rescue force - Perry.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has decided in principle that the United States will take part in a international military relief force in Zaire, Defense Secretary William Perry said on Wednesday.
"The president has decided in principle that the United States will participate in a multinational relief force," Perry told reporters.

Perry said the U.S. planned to send in about 1,000 troops to the eastern Zaire town of Goma to secure and run the airport, the key center for distributing relief. A smaller number would be sent to nearby countries to handle the airlift. An infantry battalion on the ground and helicopters would be sent to ensure the U.S. miission was protected.
Perry said the multinational force force would be under the command of a Canadian general, with an American general as the deputy commander.

He stressed the U.S. decision to participate in the force was contingent on securing commitments from African countries involved, principally Zaire and Rwanda, not to interfere with the mission. "Our assumption is that we would have their acquiesence," he said.

In addition Perry, speaking after receiving an achievement award from the defense industry, said there would be discussions in coming days with other countries involved on a number of other issues, including a clear definition of the mission, an exit strategy and the command structure.
